heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Croatia
heroData.subtitle: Hire compliant teams in Croatia without a local entity
heroData.description: Expand into Croatia's growing economy by hiring local talent legally and efficiently. Our Employer of Record (EOR) services manage payroll, social security, and local labor law compliance so you can focus on growth.
heroData.bestFor: Companies seeking fast market entry and cost-effective hiring

steps.title: Documentation Gathering
steps.description: Collect the employee's National ID (Osobna iskaznica), OIB (Tax Number), and proof of education. For foreign nationals, a valid work and residence permit (Dozvola za boravak i rad) is required.

steps.title: Mandatory Medical Examination
steps.description: Croatian law requires a 'prethodni zdravstveni pregled' for specific roles (especially those with increased risk) before the employee starts working.

steps.title: Employment Contract Drafting
steps.description: Prepare a written contract in Croatian (bilingual recommended). Contracts can be for an Indefinite term (default) or Fixed-term (max 3 years, with specific justifications).

steps.title: Registration with Social Security
steps.description: Submit the M-1P form to HZMO (Pension Insurance) and the M-1C form to HZZO (Health Insurance). This MUST be done no later than the day employment begins, before the first hour of work.

steps.title: Workplace Safety Training
steps.description: Provide mandatory occupational health and safety training (Zaštita na radu) as required by the Croatian Occupational Safety and Health Act.

items.title: Probationary Period
items.text: The maximum statutory probation period is 6 months. During this time, the notice period for contract termination is at least 7 days.

items.title: Standard Working Hours
items.text: Full-time work is 40 hours per week. Overtime is limited to 10 hours per week, 180 hours per year (unless stipulated otherwise in a collective agreement).

items.title: Final Payment Deadline
items.text: Upon termination, the employer must provide the final paycheck and all related documents within 8 days of the end of employment.

items.title: Notice Periods
items.text: Standard notice periods range from 2 weeks for less than 1 year of service to 3 months for 20+ years of service.

items.title: Annual Paid Leave
items.description: Employees are entitled to a minimum of 4 weeks (20 working days) of paid annual leave per year, assuming a 5-day work week.

items.title: Sick Leave
items.description: Sick leave (Bolovanje) for the first 42 days is paid by the employer (usually 70-85% of salary). From the 43rd day, the cost is reimbursed by HZZO.

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.description: Mandatory maternity leave is 98 days (28 days before birth, 70 days after). Total leave can extend significantly with parental leave options.

items.title: Public Holiday Pay
items.description: Work on public holidays (14 days in Croatia) is entitled to increased pay, often 50% or more depending on the collective agreement.

items.title: Fixed-Term Abuses
items.text: Using fixed-term contracts without valid legal reasons (e.g., project-based work) can lead to the contract being legally reclassified as indefinite.

items.title: Vacation Carryover
items.text: Employees must use at least 2 weeks of vacation in the current year. The rest can be carried over but must be used by June 30th of the following year.

items.title: Medical Check Delays
items.text: Failing to conduct the mandatory medical exam before the start date can lead to significant fines during a labor inspection.

faqs.question: Can I hire remote contractors through an EOR in Croatia?
faqs.answer: Yes, but if the relationship resembles employment (subordination, fixed hours), it's safer to use an EOR to hire them as full-time employees to avoid misclassification risks.

faqs.question: Is a 13th-month salary mandatory in Croatia?
faqs.answer: No, a 13th-month salary is not legally required. However, it is common to provide 'Božićnica' (Christmas bonus) or 'Uskrsnica' (Easter bonus) as a benefit.

faqs.question: Can an EOR sponsor work permits in Croatia?
faqs.answer: Yes, high-quality EOR providers can assist with the application for residence and work permits (Dozvola za boravak i rad) for foreign talent.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period for terminating an EOR agreement?
faqs.answer: Standard agreements usually specify 30 to 90 days, aligning with Croatian labor law requirements and the level of the roles involved.

faqs.question: Are health insurance benefits included in EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, mandatory state health insurance is covered via social security contributions. Supplemental private health insurance can also be offered as an additional benefit.

faqs.question: How are expense reimbursements handled?
faqs.answer: Business expenses are processed alongside the monthly payroll, ensuring they comply with non-taxable limits set by Croatian tax authorities.

steps.title: Gross Salary Calculation
steps.description: Consolidating base salary, bonuses, and taxable allowances. Calculations are performed in EUR following the 2025 exchange rules.

steps.title: Social Contribution Withholding
steps.description: Deducting 20% for Pension Insurance (Employee) and calculating 16.5% Health Insurance (Employer) on Gross salary I.

steps.title: Personal Income Tax (PIT) Application
steps.description: Applying the progressive tax rates (15% to 33% depending on city) after subtracting the personal allowance and pension contributions.

steps.title: JOPPD Form Submission
steps.description: Submitting the mandatory electronic report (JOPPD) to the Tax Administration on the day of salary payment or the day after.

steps.title: Net Disbursement
steps.description: Disbursement of net salaries to employees' EUR bank accounts and filing of tax/contribution payments to the state.

items.title: Abolition of Surtax (Prirez)
items.text: Effective January 1, 2024, the local surtax (prirez) was abolished. Municipalities now have the power to set their own income tax rates within statutory ranges.

items.title: Personal Allowance
items.text: The monthly personal allowance (non-taxable base) has been increased in 2025 to support lower-income earners, typically around €600+ depending on dependents.

items.title: Non-Taxable Benefits
items.text: Employers can provide specific non-taxable bonuses such as meal allowances (€100/mo), transport reimbursements, and annual performance bonuses up to certain caps.

items.title: Salary Payment Date
items.text: Salaries must be paid by the 15th of the month for the previous month. Most professional firms pay between the 1st and 10th.

items.title: JOPPD Reporting
items.text: Electronic reporting to the Tax Administration is mandatory via the ePorezna portal on the day of payment.

items.title: Public Holiday Shift
items.text: If the 15th falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline for payroll payment is usually the last preceding business day.

items.title: A1 Certificates
items.text: For EU employees working temporarily in Croatia, an A1 certificate is essential to remain covered by their home country's social security system.

items.title: Net-to-Gross Agreements
items.text: While common in expat packages, net-to-gross agreements must be carefully handled in payroll to account for variable municipal tax rates.

items.title: Housing & Benefits
items.text: Employer-provided housing or car benefits are taxable as personal income and must be grossed up and included in the monthly JOPPD reporting.

faqs.question: Are payslips required to be in Croatian?
faqs.answer: Yes, payslips must be issued in Croatian. However, for international teams, providing a bilingual version is best practice.

faqs.question: How are sick leave payments shared?
faqs.answer: The employer pays for the first 42 days (min 70% of average salary). Compensation from the 43rd day is paid by HZZO, though the employer often pays and then seeks reimbursement.

faqs.question: Is digital filing of the JOPPD form mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, the JOPPD form must be submitted electronically to the Tax Administration for every single payment of income to an individual.

faqs.question: Can we pay salaries in US Dollars?
faqs.answer: No, all salaries must be paid in Euro (EUR) into a bank account. Foreign currency payments are generally not permitted for local employment contracts.

steps.title: Gross I Input
steps.description: Enter the base monthly salary in EUR before any employee deductions.

steps.title: Pension Deductions
steps.description: The calculator automatically deducts 20% total (15% Pillar I + 5% Pillar II) from Gross I.

steps.title: Personal Allowance
steps.description: Subtracting the basic personal allowance (approx €600) and any additional credits for children or dependents.

steps.title: Income Tax Calculation
steps.description: Applying the lower (15-23%) or higher (25-33%) PIT rate based on the taxable base and the employee's municipality.

steps.title: Total Cost Output
steps.description: Adding the 16.5% Health Insurance to Gross I to calculate the 'Total Employer Cost' (Gross II).

items.title: Nutrition Allowance
items.text: Non-taxable meal stipends (up to €100/mo) can be added to net salary without increasing the tax base.

items.title: Commuting Reimbursement
items.text: Public transport costs are non-taxable when paid according to actual public transit prices or specific per-km rates.

items.title: Occasional Bonuses
items.text: Traditional bonuses (Božićnica, Uskrsnica) up to annual limits are non-taxable and should be included in total net planning.

faqs.question: Does this calculator include the 2025 city tax changes?
faqs.answer: Yes, our logic is updated to reflect the abolition of separate 'prirez' and its integration into the new municipal PIT rates for 2025.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Gross I and Gross II?
faqs.answer: Gross I is the employee's gross pay before their 20% pension deduction. Gross II includes the additional 16.5% health insurance paid by the employer.

faqs.question: Can I calculate part-time salaries?
faqs.answer: Yes, the tax and contribution calculations apply proportionally to the gross amount earned, regardless of full-time or part-time status.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Croatia
heroData.subtitle: Establish your d.o.o. or branch in Croatia
heroData.description: Unlock the European market with a Croatian legal entity. Our experts guide you through the process of setting up a Limited Liability Company (d.o.o.), from notary appointments to tax registration.
heroData.bestFor: Foreign investors and entrepreneurs entering the SEE region

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Check and reserve the company name at the FINA (Financial Agency) or directly at the Commercial Court via the 'sudski registar' portal.

steps.title: Notarization of Documents
steps.description: Draft and notarize the Articles of Association (Izjava o osnivanju) and the Statement of Acceptance of Appointment by the Director.

steps.title: Share Capital Deposit
steps.description: Deposit the minimum share capital (€2,500 for a d.o.o.) into a temporary account at a local Croatian bank. Obtain a certificate of deposit.

steps.title: Court Registration
steps.description: Submit all documents to the Commercial Court (Trgovački sud). Registration is typically processed within 3-7 business days.

steps.title: Tax & Statistical Registration
steps.description: Apply for an OIB (Personal Identification Number) and register with the Central Bureau of Statistics (E-obrt/E-tvrtka).

items.title: Standard d.o.o.
items.text: Limited Liability Company. Best for most businesses. Minimum capital €2,500. Required for employing non-EU nationals under specific quotas.

items.title: Simple j.d.o.o.
items.text: Simplified LLC. Capital as low as €1.33. Restricted profit distribution rules until reserves reach €2,500. Often insufficient for work permits.

items.title: Branch Office (Podružnica)
items.text: Not a separate legal entity. The parent company carries full liability. Easier to set up for existing EU companies.

items.title: VAT Registration
items.description: Mandatory if annual revenue exceeds €40,000 (PDV). Voluntary registration is possible from day one.

items.title: Company Stamp
items.description: While increasingly optional in the EU, a physical company stamp ('pečat') is still widely used and often expected in Croatian administrative dealings.

items.title: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
items.description: Mandatory registration of the ultimate owner in the Croatian UBO register (Registar stvarnih vlasnika) within 30 days.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, every Croatian company must have a registered office address. Virtual offices are legal and commonly used by foreign investors.

faqs.question: Can I open a company remotely?
faqs.answer: Partially. Documents must be notarized, which often requires a visit or a Power of Attorney (PoA) certified with an Apostille.

heroData.bestFor: Growing teams and specialized skill sourcing

steps.title: Talent Sourcing
steps.description: Utilizing popular local platforms like MojPosao and LinkedIn to source both active and passive candidates in the SEE region.

steps.title: Technical & Cultural Screening
steps.description: Multi-stage interviews including language proficiency checks (English/German are common second languages in Croatia).

steps.title: Work Permit Sponsorship (Non-EU)
steps.description: Processing applications for the 'Dozvola za boravak i rad' via the MUP (Ministry of Interior) under the 2025 streamlined rules.

steps.title: Reference & Background Checks
steps.description: Verifying educational credentials and professional history in compliance with Croatian privacy laws.

steps.title: Contract Execution
steps.description: Issuing formal offer letters and employment contracts that specify the base salary in EUR and all statutory benefits.

items.title: Tech Talent Hub
items.text: Zagreb and Split have emerged as significant tech hubs in the Mediterranean, with a strong pool of software engineers and digital specialists.

items.title: Foreigners Act 2025
items.text: New regulations introduced in March 2025 require employers to demonstrate a clean tax record and specific housing standards when hiring non-EU workers.

items.title: Salary Expectations
items.text: Gross salaries in Croatia are rising. IT roles typically range from €2,500 to €6,000+ Gross I, depending on seniority.

items.title: Equal Treatment
items.description: Agency workers must be provided the same basic working and employment conditions as if they were hired directly by the user undertaking.

items.title: Contract Duration
items.description: The assignment of a worker to a single user undertaking via an agency is generally limited to a maximum of 3 consecutive years.

items.title: Liability
items.description: The user undertaking and the agency are jointly liable for specific labor obligations, emphasizing the need for licensed agency partners.

faqs.question: What is the typical time-to-hire in Croatia?
faqs.answer: For technical roles, it usually takes 4-8 weeks. Standard administrative or commercial roles can often be filled within 3-5 weeks.

faqs.question: Are there specific platforms for tech hiring in Croatia?
faqs.answer: Yes, localized platforms like MojPosao and Posao.hr are very effective, alongside LinkedIn and tech-focused communities like Joberty.

faqs.question: Is it common to use headhunters for executive roles?
faqs.answer: Yes, executive search agencies are highly active in Zagreb and are commonly used for C-suite and senior management positions.

faqs.question: Are background checks legal in Croatia?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they must be relevant to the job and comply with GDPR. Criminal record checks are only allowed for specific roles (e.g., finance, working with children).

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions in Croatia
heroData.subtitle: Centralize and automate your HR operations locally
heroData.description: Modernize your workforce management with HRIS tools tailored for Croatian businesses. Ensure GDPR compliance while managing employee lifecycles and time-tracking digitally.

steps.title: Localization Setup
steps.description: Configuring the system to handle Croatian public holidays, currency (EUR), and local date formats.

steps.title: Data Privacy Mapping
steps.description: Ensuring all personal data processing flows comply with GDPR and the Croatian Act on the Implementation of the General Data Protection Regulation.

steps.title: Internal Communication
steps.description: Setting up the employee self-service portal for leave requests, document access, and expense management.

steps.title: Payroll Bridge Activation
steps.description: Mapping HR data to payroll variables to ensure seamless generation of JOPPD reports and payslips.

items.title: Electronic Records
items.text: Croatian Labor Law permits electronic keeping of employee records, provided the integrity and accessibility of data are maintained for inspections.

items.title: Digital Signatures
items.text: Electronic signatures are increasingly accepted. Advanced electronic signatures (AdES) are recommended for formal employee notices and contract addendums.

items.title: AZOP Oversight
items.text: The Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP) enforces strict privacy rules. HR platforms must have robust audit trails and access controls.

items.title: Time and Attendance
items.description: Automated tracking of working hours, necessary for calculating overtime and shift differentials according to local law.

items.title: Leave Management
items.description: Digital workflows for approving annual leave, sick leave (requiring medical 'doznaka'), and personal days.

items.title: Document Centralization
items.description: Secure storage of employment contracts, NDAs, and workplace safety certificates.

items.title: Personnel Records
items.description: Systematic tracking of employee data required for the 'Evidencija o radnicima' according to the Ministry of Labor regulations.

items.title: Statistical Reports
items.description: Simplified generation of data for the 'RAD-1' and 'RAD-1G' forms required by the Croatian Bureau of Statistics.

items.title: Gender Pay Gap
items.description: Increasingly important analytics for large companies to comply with evolving EU transparency directives and local expectations.

faqs.question: Can we host our HR data outside of Croatia?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the data remains within the EEA or in a country with adequate protection, and you have a valid Data Processing Agreement (DPA) in place.

faqs.question: Is integration with local payroll providers possible?
faqs.answer: Yes, most modern HRIS platforms can be integrated with local Croatian payroll systems via API or regular flat-file exports.

faqs.question: Does the system need to support the Croatian language?
faqs.answer: While not strictly mandatory for internal use, providing a Croatian interface is highly recommended for employee engagement and legal clarity during audits.

faqs.question: Is it easy to integrate local payroll with global HRIS platforms?
faqs.answer: Most modern HRIS (like Workday or HiBob) can integrate via API or flat-file exchange with local Croatian payroll providers.

heroData.title: Accounting Services in Croatia
heroData.subtitle: Professional bookkeeping and financial reporting
heroData.description: Keep your Croatian entity compliant with HSFI and IFRS standards. Our accounting partners handle daily bookkeeping, tax filings, and annual audits with precision.

steps.title: Monthly Bookkeeping
steps.description: Recording all transactions, bank reconciliations, and expense processing in accordance with Croatian accounting laws.

steps.title: VAT Reporting
steps.description: Preparing and submitting the monthly or quarterly PDV report to the Tax Administration by the 20th of the following month.

steps.title: Financial Statement Drafting
steps.description: Compiling Profit & Loss statements and Balance Sheets under Croatian Financial Reporting Standards (HSFI).

steps.title: Annual Filing (GFI)
steps.description: Submitting the Annual Financial Report to FINA (Financial Agency) for public disclosure purposes by April 30.

steps.title: Audit Coordination
steps.description: Facilitating external audits for large entities or those meeting specific revenue/asset thresholds.

items.title: B2G E-Invoicing
items.description: Since 2019, all invoices to government entities must be sent electronically via the FINA e-Račun portal.

items.title: Fiscalization
items.description: Real-time reporting of cash transactions to the Tax Administration is mandatory for retail and service providers.

items.title: Internal Controls
items.description: Implementation of digital approval workflows to ensure transaction validity and audit readiness.

items.title: Statutory Audit Thresholds
items.text: Audits are mandatory for large and medium-sized entities. Thresholds include assets over €2M, revenue over €4M, or more than 50 employees.

items.title: Public Disclosure
items.text: All registered companies must publish their annual financial statements on the FINA portal, making certain financial data accessible to the public.

items.title: HSFI Compliance
items.text: Small and micro entities use the Croatian Financial Reporting Standards (HSFI), which are simplified but still strictly enforced by the Tax Administration.

faqs.question: What is the standard VAT rate in Croatia?
faqs.answer: The standard PDV rate is 25%. Reduced rates of 13% and 5% apply to specific goods and services like accommodation, books, and basic foods.

faqs.question: How long must I keep accounting records?
faqs.answer: Invoices and bookkeeping documents must be kept for at least 11 years. Payroll records and personnel files must be kept permanently.

faqs.question: Can I use US GAAP for my Croatian subsidiary?
faqs.answer: For local statutory filing, you MUST use HSFI (or IFRS for large entities). You can maintain US GAAP records for group reporting separately.

steps.title: KYC & AML Screening
steps.description: Verifying partners and clients against international and local sanction lists according to Croatian AML laws.

steps.title: UBO Register Filing
steps.description: Identifying and registering ultimate beneficial owners in the state-held register managed by FINA.

steps.title: Data Privacy Audit
steps.description: Reviewing data processing activities for GDPR compliance and ensuring local 'Pravilnik o privatnosti' is in place.

steps.title: Workplace Safety Audit
steps.description: Annual assessment of health and safety protocols to maintain certificates required by the Labor Inspectorate.

items.title: AZOP Enforcement
items.text: The Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP) has increased inspections, focusing on consumer rights and employee surveillance transparency.

items.title: Legal Basis for Processing
items.text: Consent is just one of several legal bases; contract performance and legitimate interest are frequently more appropriate for B2B operations.

items.title: DPO Appointment
items.text: While not mandatory for all, appointing a Data Protection Officer is standard practice for firms processing high volumes of personal data.

items.title: Statistical Reporting
items.description: Periodic surveys from the Central Bureau of Statistics on foreign trade, salaries, and staffing levels.

items.title: Environmental Levies
items.description: Reporting to the Fund for Environmental Protection on packaging and waste management if applicable.

items.title: Foreign Exchange Reporting
items.description: Requirements to report specific cross-border transactions to the Croatian National Bank (HNB).

items.title: Real-time Reporting
items.text: In-scope transactions must be reported to the tax server instantly. Software must be certified for the Croatian 'fiskalizacija' protocol.

items.title: Cash Payment Limits
items.text: There are strict limits on cash transactions between business entities (typically limited to €5,000) to prevent money laundering.

items.title: Digital Certificate
items.text: Every business entity must obtain a specific digital certificate from FINA to sign and send fiscalized invoices to the Tax Administration.

faqs.question: What are the penalties for GDPR non-compliance in Croatia?
faqs.answer: Penalties follow the EU-wide GDPR framework, with fines reaching up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher.

faqs.question: Do we need a physical office in Croatia for compliance?
faqs.answer: While a registered address is mandatory, many administrative functions can be managed remotely with the help of a local representative or EOR.

faqs.question: Are environmental reports required for software companies?
faqs.answer: Generally no, unless the company imports electronic equipment or produces significant physical waste falling under specific waste management regulations.

steps.title: Monthly PIT Withholding
steps.description: Calculating and remitting Personal Income Tax on behalf of employees simultaneously with salary payments.

steps.title: VAT (PDV) Preparation
steps.description: Compiling input and output VAT records to file monthly returns by the 20th of the following month (standard deadline).

steps.title: CIT Prepayment Estimation
steps.description: Calculating monthly Corporate Income Tax prepayments based on the previous year's profitability.

steps.title: Annual Tax Reconciliation
steps.description: Finalizing the annual Corporate Income Tax return (Form PD) by April 30th for the previous calendar year.

items.title: New PIT Brackets 2025
items.text: Municipal reforms have updated the income thresholds for the 33% higher tax rate, now adjusted to account for inflation and cost of living.

items.title: Crypto Asset Taxation
items.text: Profits from cryptocurrency trading are treated as capital income (12%), provided assets are held for less than two years.

items.title: Foreign Income Reporting
items.text: Croatian tax residents must report worldwide income, though double taxation treaties with 60+ countries often mitigate additional liability.

items.title: R&D Tax Deductions
items.description: Companies can reduce their taxable base by up to 150-200% of eligible Research and Development expenditure.

items.title: Investment Incentives
items.description: Reduced CIT rates (as low as 0%) for major investments that create new employment in assisted regions.

items.title: Youth Employment Relief
items.description: Full or partial exemption from certain social contributions for hiring workers under the age of 30 for their first permanent role.

items.title: Network of Treaties
items.text: Croatia has signed over 65 double tax treaties, including with the US, UK, and most EU nations, to prevent double taxation of income and capital.

items.title: Withholding Tax Reductions
items.text: Treaties often reduce the standard withholding tax on dividends (12%) and royalties/interest (15%) for residents of treaty countries.

items.title: PE Risk Management
items.text: Guidelines on Permanent Establishment (PE) follow OECD patterns, defining when a foreign company's activities in Croatia trigger local corporate tax.

faqs.question: What is the tax year in Croatia?
faqs.answer: The tax year is the calendar year. However, companies can request a different fiscal year if it matches their parent company's cycle.

faqs.question: When is the deadline for personal income tax returns?
faqs.answer: Most individual income tax is settled via withholding. For those required to file (e.g., self-employed), the deadline is typically the end of February.

faqs.question: Is there a wealth tax in Croatia?
faqs.answer: No, Croatia does not currently impose a general wealth tax, though there are specific taxes on vacation homes and motor vehicles.

heroData.bestFor: B2B service providers and technology firms

steps.title: Entity Verification
steps.description: Checking the counterparty against the Sudski Registar to confirm valid registration and OIB.

steps.title: Authority Check
steps.description: Verifying that the signatories have the legal right to bind the company (Director vs Prokurist).

steps.title: Drafting & Localization
steps.description: Adapting global templates to include mandatory Croatian provisions on payments, termination, and liability.

steps.title: Execution & Notarization
steps.description: Signing the document. Specific agreements (e.g., real estate or large loans) require solemnization by a Notary Public.

items.title: Civil Law Tradition
items.text: Croatia follows the Civil Law tradition, based primarily on encoded statutes like the Law on Obligations (ZOO).

items.title: Choice of Law
items.text: While international parties can often choose foreign law, mandatory Croatian rules (e.g., labor, real estate) will always prevail for local operations.

items.title: Enforcement Timelines
items.text: Resolution of commercial disputes in Croatian courts can be lengthy; including arbitration clauses (e.g., HGK) is often recommended.

items.title: Intellectual Property
items.description: Explicit assignment of IP rights created during the service term to the buyer, adhering to the Copyright and Related Rights Act.

items.title: Termination for Cause
items.description: Defining specific breaches (e.g., non-payment, insolvency) that allow for immediate contract dissolution.

items.title: Liability Caps
items.description: Negotiating reasonable limits on damages, excluding gross negligence or willful misconduct as per local law.

items.title: Choice of Law
items.text: Parties can choose a foreign law for international contracts, but mandatory Croatian labor and real estate laws cannot be bypassed for local operations.

items.title: Litigation Timelines
items.text: Commercial litigation in Croatian courts can be slow. Including an arbitration clause (e.g., Zagreb Rules) is often recommended for faster resolution.

items.title: Enforcement of Judgments
items.text: As an EU member, Croatia follows the Brussels I Regulation for the recognition and enforcement of judgments from other EU member states.

faqs.question: Are oral contracts valid in Croatia?
faqs.answer: While generally valid for some commercial dealings, most significant contracts (employment, real estate, company formation) MUST be in writing to be enforceable.

faqs.question: Do I need a local legal representative?
faqs.answer: For foreign entities without a local director, appointing a local proxy or legal representative is highly recommended for administrative and court dealings.

faqs.question: What is the standard notice period for B2B contract termination?
faqs.answer: If not specified, the Law on Obligations dictates a 'reasonable' period, but market standard is typically 30 to 90 days.

faqs.question: Is IP ownership clearly protected in Croatia?
faqs.answer: Yes, Croatian law provides strong IP protection. Standard contracts ensure that all work-for-hire IP is automatically transferred to the client.

faqs.question: What is the English proficiency level in the IT sector?
faqs.answer: Very high. Most Croatian developers have professional working proficiency in English, as it is the primary language for technical education and global work.

faqs.question: Are there any tax incentives for young employees in Croatia?
faqs.answer: Yes, employees under 25 are exempt from 100% of income tax on their salary, and those aged 25-30 are exempt from 50% of the income tax.

faqs.question: What is the corporate tax rate for small businesses?
faqs.answer: Companies with annual revenues up to €1 million pay a reduced corporate income tax rate of 10%. Above that, the standard rate is 18%.
